prompt:

Keep the near-camera framing role, general cluster locations and similar overall foreground coverage. The cosmos must remain visible as close-up flowers rather than being removed or reduced to distant dots. Let individual cosmos heads be naturally somewhat smaller and airier than lily blooms, with several gracefully spaced blossoms at varied heights and a few small unopened buds. Keep the central view across the lawn unobstructed.
COSMOS DESIGN: elegant open daisy-like discs with roughly eight broad thin petals, subtly notched or gently scalloped tips, soft radial folds and modest small yellow centers; long slender slightly curving stems, delicate finely divided feathery cosmos foliage. Mixed three-quarter, frontal and side-facing flower orientations make the arrangement relaxed and natural. Flowers are lightly spaced, not stiff identical repeated discs or a dense wall of petals. Avoid lilies, roses, heavy layered petal whorls, huge dark centers, thick fleshy petals, rigid plastic flowers or giant graphic clip-art daisies. STYLE: refined hand-painted 2D Japanese anime / visual-novel background illustration, with attractive clean petal silhouettes, graceful delicate contour accents, simplified intentional painted colour planes and restrained soft gradients. Cosmos should feel light, airy and romantic. Preserve realistic light physics: the input's same warm afternoon sun direction, subtle translucent petals, soft shading and gentle cast shadows; keep highlight detail in the white petals. No photographic microtexture, no 3D flower rendering, no crude flat symbols or excessive bloom.
LOCK THE REST OF THE IMAGE: leave all distant and midground roses and other flowers unchanged. Preserve exactly the existing old stone wall and arch geometry, the scene visible through the right-hand arch, the tree trunk and canopy, rose trellis, two chairs and cushions, small table, all background plants, central lawn outline, grass, stone paths, composition, colour grading and the existing dappled sunlight. The task is ONLY to compare a cosmos foreground against the previous lily version. Do not redesign the garden or modify distant architecture, flowers or furniture. Do not add banners, heraldry, statues, water features, doorways, people, text or UI. Keep the camera at the same eye-level position, no wider crop, no elevated view. Outside the two foreground flower clusters and their immediate stems/leaves, preserve the base image as faithfully as possible.
